stem: A borrower receives a loan repaid through four equal annual instalments of Rs 3,000 at the end of each year. The lender charges 8% per annum compound interest. What is the present value of these instalments (i.e., the original loan amount)?  [Given: (1.08)^4 = 1.3605, so (1.08)^(-4) = 0.7350]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Adding four payments of Rs 3,000 without discounting gives Rs 12,000, ignoring the time value of money.
Multiplying the ordinary-annuity PV by (1.08) as if the payments started at the beginning of the period gives Rs 9,937.50 x 1.08 = Rs 10,732.50, the annuity-due formula applied incorrectly here.
Using the FV formula instead of PV gives 3000 x (1.3605 - 1)/0.08 = 3000 x 4.5063 = Rs 13,518.75, which is the future value, not the present value.

explanation: The present value of an ordinary annuity is PV = A x [1 - (1+i)^(-n)] / i. With A = Rs 3,000, i = 0.08, n = 4 and (1.08)^(-4) = 0.7350: PV = 3000 x (1-0.7350)/0.08 = 3000 x 3.3125 = Rs 9,937.50.

explanation_sections.punchline: The loan amount equals the present value of all future repayments discounted at the lending rate - use PV = A x [1-(1+i)^(-n)]/i.
explanation_sections.lesson: PV uses the discount factor [1-(1+i)^(-n)] whereas FV uses [(1+i)^n - 1]; choosing the wrong one gives the right formula applied to the wrong direction.
explanation_sections.timing: 80 seconds. Identify PV formula, plug in the given inverse power, compute. Trap: option 4 uses FV formula.
